net.text: Included in "Results of Operations" below for the three and nine months ended May 31, 2025 compared to the comparable prior year period is a reconciliation of EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA from net income, the most directly comparable GAAP measure. We have included these non-GAAP performance measures as a comparable measure to illustrate the effect of non-recurring transactions that occurred during the reported periods and to improve comparability of our results from period to period. We believe Adjusted EBITDA provides meaningful supplemental information about our operating performance as this measure excludes amounts from net income that we do not consider part of our core operating results when assessing our performance. Examples of items excluded from Adjusted EBITDA include acquisition-related costs, change in fair value of note receivable, contingent consideration fair value adjustment, loss on note repurchase, asset impairment, and non-operating income or loss.

capex.heading: Capital Expenditures
capex.text: We anticipate capital expenditures in Fiscal 2026 of approximately $35.0 million to $45.0 million. We will continue to support organic growth through facility improvements to benefit a safer operating environment, operational improvements, and investments in software and our digital capabilities. We believe cash on hand, funds generated from operations, and the borrowing capacity available under our ABL Credit Facility and other debt instruments will be sufficient to support our capital expenditures for the foreseeable future.

intro.text: The use of the terms "Winnebago Industries," "Winnebago," "we," "our," and "us" in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, unless the context otherwise requires, refer to Winnebago Industries, Inc. and its wholly-owned subsidiaries. Winnebago Industries, Inc. is a leading North American manufacturer of outdoor lifestyle products under the Winnebago, Grand Design, Chris-Craft, Newmar and Barletta brands, which are used primarily in leisure travel and outdoor recreation activities. We also design and manufacture advanced battery solutions that deliver “house power,” supporting internal electrical features and appliances for a variety of outdoor products including RVs, boats, specialty and other low-speed vehicles, as well as other industrial applications. Other products manufactured by us consist primarily of original equipment manufacturing parts for other manufacturers and commercial vehicles.

metrics.label: Accrual ratio

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

gp.text: Gross profit as a percentage of revenue decreased primarily due to deleverage and slightly higher warranty experience.

oi.text: Operating income margin decreased primarily due to deleverage, including that associated with product mix, and higher warranty experience.

opex.text: Operating expenses decreased primarily due to prior year goodwill impairment and cost reduction initiatives in the current year, partially offset by investments to support the growth of the Grand Design motorhome and Barletta marine businesses.

costs.text: Operating expenses decreased primarily due to prior year goodwill impairment and cost reduction initiatives in the current year, partially offset by investments to support the growth of the Grand Design motorhome and Barletta marine businesses.

tax.text: Our effective tax rate decreased primarily due to the prior year's non-deductible debt inducement loss and non-deductible goodwill impairment and, in Fiscal 2025, increased favorable return to provision adjustments and reduced change in the valuation allowance over lower pre-tax income.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: During Fiscal 2025, cash provided by operating activities was $128.9 million compared to $143.9 million in Fiscal 2024. The decrease in operating cash flow is primarily driven by lower profitability adjusted for non-cash items, an increase in accounts receivable due to timing of invoicing and collections, unfavorable changes in accounts payable balances and timing of payments, partially offset by improvement in inventory levels and operational efficiency actions.

wc.heading: Working Capital
wc.text: Working capital as of August 30, 2025 and August 31, 2024 was $465.1 million and $584.0 million, respectively. We currently expect cash on hand, funds generated from operations, and the borrowing available under our ABL Credit Facility to be sufficient to cover both short-term and long-term operating requirements.

capex.heading: Capital Expenditures
capex.text: We anticipate capital expenditures in Fiscal 2026 of approximately $35.0 million to $45.0 million. We will continue to support organic growth through facility improvements to benefit a safer operating environment, operational improvements, and investments in software and our digital capabilities. We believe cash on hand, funds generated from operations, and the borrowing capacity available under our ABL Credit Facility and other debt instruments will be sufficient to support our capital expenditures for the foreseeable future.

oi.text: Operating income as a percentage of revenues decreased primarily due to volume deleverage, higher discounts and allowances, and product mix, partially offset by selective price adjustments and cost containment initiatives.

opex.text: Operating expenses decreased primarily due to cost reduction initiatives, partially offset by costs to support the growth of the Grand Design Motorhome business.

costs.text: Operating expenses decreased primarily due to cost reduction initiatives, partially offset by costs to support the growth of the Grand Design Motorhome business.

tax.text: The increase in the effective tax rate was primarily driven by current year state tax adjustments, increased valuation allowances, and a reduced benefit from favorable items due to higher pre-tax income.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: During Fiscal 2026, cash provided by operating activities was $168.7 million compared to $128.9 million in Fiscal 2025. The change in operating cash flow is primarily driven by higher profitability adjusted for non-cash items, favorable changes in accounts receivable and accounts payable balances due to timing of receipts and payments, partially offset by changes in inventory levels.

wc.heading: Working Capital
wc.text: Working capital as of August 29, 2026 and August 30, 2025 was $419.1 million and $465.1 million, respectively. We currently expect cash on hand, funds generated from operations, and the borrowing available under our ABL Credit Facility to be sufficient to cover both short-term and long-term operating requirements.

capex.heading: Capital Expenditures
capex.text: We anticipate capital expenditures in Fiscal 2027 of approximately $35.0 million to $45.0 million. We will continue to support organic growth through facility improvements to support a safe operating environment, operational improvements, and investments in software and our digital capabilities. We believe cash on hand, funds generated from operations, and the borrowing capacity available under our ABL Credit Facility and other debt instruments will be sufficient to support our capital expenditures for the foreseeable future.

Such conditions may also cause consumers to delay, reduce or forgo purchases of our products and may lead dealers to reduce inventory levels, delay replenishment orders, increase promotional activity or otherwise reduce purchases from us.
As of August 29, 2026, one financial flooring institution held approximately 33% of our total outstanding financed dealer inventory dollars.
Our business depends on the performance and financial condition of independent dealers.
We rely on our dealers to develop and implement effective strategies to create retail demand for our products and to provide quality post-sale service and support.

For some of the components used in production, we depend on a small group of suppliers and the loss of any of these suppliers could affect our ability to obtain components timely or at competitive prices, which would decrease our results of operations, financial condition, and cash flows.
In Fiscal 2026, one of our suppliers individually accounted for approximately 12% of our consolidated raw material purchases.
In the case of motorhome RV chassis, Mercedes-Benz (USA and Canada), Stellantis N.V., Freightliner Trucks, Ford Motor Company, and Spartan RV Chassis are our major suppliers.
Sales of motorhome RVs rely on chassis supply and are affected by shortages, instability, or recalls from time to time.

Furthermore, decisions by our suppliers to decrease production or increase prices, production delays or work stoppages by the employees of such suppliers, or financial distress, including bankruptcy or insolvency, of one or more key suppliers could have a material adverse effect on our ability to produce our products and ultimately on our results of operations, financial condition, and cash flows.
Our ability to respond effectively to such events depends on the adequacy of our crisis and emergency management procedures, including escalation protocols and coordination across facilities.

If the inventory levels of our dealers are higher than they desire, they may postpone product purchases from us, which could cause our sales to be lower than the end-user retail demand for our products and negatively impact our inventory management and working capital goals as well as our operating results.
In addition, we rely on our ability to adjust production capacity through overtime, additional hiring, shortened work weeks, and headcount reductions in response to changes in demand.
Additionally, we rely on information systems to record and report our operational results.
The effectiveness of AI technologies depends on the quality, availability, security, and integrity of the data on which they are trained or operate.
We also rely on third-party providers for certain AI-enabled technologies and services.
Our success in maintaining, extending, and expanding our brand image depends on our ability to adapt to a rapidly changing media environment.
We elected to rely on a qualitative assessment for the Newmar and Lithionics reporting units, and performed a quantitative analysis for the Grand Design and Barletta reporting units.
We elected to rely on a qualitative assessment for the Newmar trade name, and performed a quantitative analysis for the Chris-Craft, Grand Design, and Barletta trade names.
